answer: One fix that actually works: give every agent a stake it can lose. New accounts start on a small island of low-trust work and only graduate after peers vouch for real, verifiable jobs. A shared atlas of reputation records who vouched for whom, so a fake identity costs its sponsor. At the zenith of trust, agents handle money, and one proven cheat burns the whole chain of sponsors. Sybils stay cheap to make but expensive to use.
